utterances.text: I don't. I apologise. Your Honours, could you please repeat your question. My concentration is not that good anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember that you were shown this clipping that was titled "Serbs, Get Ready for War"? Do you remember that? So, Mr. Ostojic, yesterday you said that this paper was an extremist paper published once in a while reports that you would rather not read. Do you remember having said that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So these reports, these articles, how could you characterise them? What was their nature? Why do you say they were so radical, so extremist?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on a short insight that I had yesterday into the copies of this publication, I made the conclusion that I made. And also, I remembered what this paper wrote about, this paper Slobodna Bosna. What I had before we yesterday inspired me to say that this was a populace press that was nothing but seeking sensationalist news.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was this paper a paper that published very aggressive articles directed against those who -- the non-Serbs, other ethnic communities?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was such articles as well. Yes, this was a very aggressive paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you disapprove of the content of these articles?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. As far as I can remember, I didn't even have the guts to read those articles. I just read the titles and subtitles. There were other people in the ministry of Bosnia and Herzegovina who had a duty to read those articles. They were employees of the sector for domestic media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you did disapprove with the content of these articles?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Ostojic, I think I understood that you have met international reporters around Banja Luka, you met with them -- you admitted having met with them, right?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to journalists, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about foreign reporters. So in the documents that were presented by the Prosecutor and that we have at tab 49, if you can look at this, please, this is what I read. This is a press release from Reuters, and this is what can be read. [In English] "'Why is Christian Europe against us? We are defending them,' said Velibor Ostojic, information minister of the self-proclaimed Bosnian Serb government. "'Islam is growing everywhere. Christian Lebanon and Cyprus have been taken over. The Armenians are being wiped out. The Muslims have finance, an ideology and most of all increasing manpower.' "Ostojic said there was a plan to create a 'Muslim corridor' linking Bosnia's Muslims with Muslim Albanians, Bulgaria's Turkish minority and Turkey itself. He quoted figures he said showed that high birth-rates would make Muslims the majority group in Bosnia by the year 2000. "'France is already swamped with Muslims. Either Europe does not realise the danger it is in, or it believes it can control Bosnian Muslim President Alija Izetbegovic in the future. "'But it will be too late. When Islam takes over a state is never reversed,' Ostojic said. 'Religious wars are very cruel.' . "Crucifix-wearing Serb soldiers claim to take their inspiration from their Orthodox faith, and across northern Bosnia Serb children wave at passing cars with the three-fingered salute said to signify the Holy Trinity." [Interpretation] So you don't contest having said this, right?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember ever having said that or ever having a -- an interview with Reuters. I said that I remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, here's my question: Do you contest having said this?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR OSTOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, thank you, Mr. Ostojic, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, this concludes your testimony, taking that the last questions of the Bench do not trigger any need for further questions by the parties. Then, Mr. Ostojic, I'd like to thank you, I usually say for coming the far way to The Hague, but of course you remained in Belgrade. But nevertheless I would like to thank you for coming to testify and to answer the questions, questions first put to you by the Bench and then by the parties, and I wish you a safe trip home again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to express my gratitude to you for having allowed me to testify in Belgrade rather than travelling afar, which would have been detrimental for my health. Still, I was able to comply with the requirements of the ICTY, and therefore I would like to once again thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn. I will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom. Mr. Harmon, you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Very quickly, Your Honour, the document that was read to Mr. Ostojic by Judge Hanoteau should have a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would not mind, we are already so beyond time, that number will be given tomorrow. By the way, it's -- yes, it's one of the documents you used. We'll go through the transcript and see that all the documents that were put to the witness will get numbers to the extent they have not received them yet. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom. But not after having thanked the technicians and interpreters for their long assistance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of July, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24
